summary: Gives a one-time interpretation of eligibility rules for the 2020-2021 IETF Nominating Committee, needed because the in-person IETF 107 meeting was cancelled. It affects only the seating of that committee. It was replaced by RFC 9389.

eli5.summary: Because a big meeting was cancelled, the rules about who can join a selection team needed a one-time explanation.

subtitle: Emergency interpretation of Nominating Committee eligibility rules when IETF 107 was cancelled.

tldr.problem: The cancellation of the in-person IETF 107 meeting due to COVID-19 created ambiguity about eligibility for the 2020-2021 Nominating Committee, which normally requires attending at least three of the last five IETF meetings.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8788 provides a one-time interpretation: IETF 107 does not count toward eligibility because no in-person meeting was held. Eligibility is based on attendance at the five most recent in-person meetings (IETFs 102, 103, 104, 105, and 106).
tldr.outcome: The interpretation allowed the Nominating Committee to be seated fairly under exceptional circumstances, while making clear this sets no precedent for future meetings.

today: RFC 8788 is a Best Current Practice providing a one-time emergency interpretation. It applied only to the 2020-2021 Nominating Committee and was superseded by RFC 9389, which updated the nominating committee procedures more broadly.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
In March 2020, the COVID-19 pandemic led to the cancellation of the in-person IETF 107 meeting. The meeting was converted to a virtual-only event with limited agenda and remote participation. This created an unexpected challenge: the Nominating Committee for 2020-2021 was to be formed between IETF 107 and IETF 108, but the standard eligibility rules—which require attending at least three of the last five IETF meetings—were now ambiguous given that one meeting was only virtual.

RFC 8788 provides a one-time clarification for this exceptional situation, applying only to the 2020-2021 NomCom cycle and not setting any precedent for future committees.
sections.eli5: A big meeting got cancelled. The IETF needed to pick its leaders. The rule about who could help pick them became unclear. This document gives a one-time answer.

sections.title: Three Proposed Interpretations
sections.content:
The IETF community discussed three ways to interpret the eligibility rules. Option 1: Do not count IETF 107 at all for eligibility, treating it as if it did not happen. Eligibility would be based on the five in-person meetings prior to it (IETFs 102 through 106). Option 2: Count virtual attendance at IETF 107 (by signing the electronic blue sheet) as meeting the eligibility criteria, so people could gain eligibility but not lose it. Option 3: Treat virtual attendance at IETF 107 the same as in-person attendance, counting IETF 107 normally so eligibility would be based on IETFs 103 through 107.

The IESG evaluated these options based on fairness to newer participants, expansion of the volunteer pool, and adherence to the spirit of the community consensus rules in BCP 10.
sections.eli5: Three ideas were proposed: ignore the cancelled meeting, let virtual people count, or count virtual as equal to in-person. The IETF leadership picked the first option.

sections.title: Decision and Scope
sections.content: The IESG chose Option 1: IETF 107 does not count toward eligibility for the 2020-2021 NomCom. The eligibility rule is modified to require attendance at three of the five most recent in-person IETF meetings, explicitly named as IETFs 102, 103, 104, 105, and 106. This interpretation applies only to the 2020-2021 NomCom and to any processes relating to NomCom eligibility before IETF 108. It does not apply to any future Nominating Committee and does not set a precedent. The IETF community committed to addressing future eligibility issues through proper revision to BCP 10 rather than relying on emergency interpretations.
sections.eli5: They chose to ignore IETF 107 entirely. Eligibility was based on the previous five in-person meetings. This one-time rule did not apply to future elections. A real update to the rules would handle future situations.

references.text: Kucherawy, M., Ed., Hinden, R., Ed., and J. Livingood, Ed., "IAB, IESG, IETF Trust, and IETF LLC Selection, Confirmation, and Recall Process: Operation of the IETF Nominating and Recall Committees", BCP 10, RFC 8713, February 2020.
